questions.text: After deploying a machine learning model to production, a company observes a gradual decline in the model‘s performance due to changing customer behavior. What is the most appropriate next step in the ML lifecycle?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Model re-training

Model re-training is the most appropriate next step when a deployed machine learning model shows declining performance due to changes in underlying data patterns, such as shifting customer behavior. Over time, the data distribution may change, leading to “model drift“ or a reduction in the model‘s ability to make accurate predictions. To address this, new data reflecting the current behavior should be collected, and the model should be re-trained using this updated dataset. This ensures that the model adapts to new trends and continues to perform well in production. Regular re-training is crucial to maintain the model‘s relevance in dynamic environments.

Incorrect

Feature engineering

Feature engineering involves creating or modifying features to improve model performance. While this can be important for improving a model initially, in the case of performance decline due to data drift, re-training the model with updated data is more appropriate than revisiting feature engineering.

Data collection

Although data collection is an important part of the process before re-training, the decline in performance here suggests that the focus should be on re-training the model using newly collected data, rather than just collecting data alone.

Hyperparameter tuning

Hyperparameter tuning involves optimizing the settings of the learning algorithm to improve performance. However, since the issue here is related to changing data patterns, re-training with updated data is more appropriate than tuning hyperparameters alone.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/machine-learning/latest/dg/retraining-models-on-new-data.html

questions.text: In a customer service application, you want to balance between creative responses and deterministic ones. Adjusting which parameter will help you control the randomness of the model‘s responses?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Temperature

Temperature is the key parameter that controls the randomness and creativity of a model's responses. A higher temperature introduces more randomness, allowing the model to generate diverse and creative responses, which can be useful in scenarios where a variety of outputs is needed. On the other hand, a lower temperature makes the model more deterministic, meaning it will generate more predictable and consistent responses. By adjusting the temperature, you can find the right balance for your customer service application, ensuring that responses are creative but still relevant and accurate.

Incorrect

Input length

Input length refers to how much context or input data the model receives. It doesn't control randomness but influences the amount of information the model can use for generating responses.

Model size

Model size refers to the complexity of the model, such as the number of layers or parameters. While it affects the model's capacity to learn and generate sophisticated outputs, it doesn't directly control the randomness of responses.

Latency

Latency is the time it takes for the model to respond, which impacts performance but not the creativity or randomness of the responses.

questions.text: A company is developing a machine learning model for supply chain optimization. They want to ensure that the model is sustainable and minimizes its environmental impact. Which of the following should be considered when selecting the model?

options.text: The number of features included in the dataset
The cost of using cloud services for the model
The model‘s energy consumption during training and inference

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

The model‘s energy consumption during training and inference

The model‘s energy consumption during training and inference is a crucial factor when aiming for sustainability and minimizing environmental impact. Machine learning models, especially complex ones, can require significant computational resources, leading to high energy usage. This not only increases operational costs but also contributes to a larger carbon footprint due to the energy consumed, often generated from non-renewable sources. By considering models that are more energy-efficient, the company can reduce the environmental impact. This can involve selecting algorithms that require less computational power, optimizing code for efficiency, or using hardware that consumes less energy. Additionally, implementing strategies like model pruning, quantization, or using more efficient data representations can further decrease energy consumption. Focusing on energy efficiency aligns with sustainable practices and supports corporate social responsibility goals, all while maintaining the effectiveness of the supply chain optimization.

Incorrect

The number of features included in the dataset

While reducing the number of features can simplify the model and potentially decrease training time, it doesn‘t directly address sustainability or environmental impact unless it significantly affects energy consumption.

The complexity of the dataset

Dataset complexity may influence the difficulty of the modeling task, but it isn‘t a primary factor in the model‘s environmental impact unless it leads to increased computational requirements.

The cost of using cloud services for the model

The cost of cloud services is a financial concern. While cost and energy consumption can be related, focusing solely on cost doesn‘t directly ensure sustainability or minimize environmental impact.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/sustainability-pillar/sustainability-pillar.html

questions.text: During the development of an AI-powered legal assistant, you want to ensure the model doesn‘t generate harmful or misleading content. What prompt engineering best practices should you implement to prevent undesirable outputs?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Applying guardrails in the prompts

Applying guardrails in the prompts involves incorporating specific instructions or constraints within your prompts to prevent the AI model from generating harmful, misleading, or undesirable content. By explicitly stating what the model should avoid or focus on, you guide it to produce responses that are safe, accurate, and appropriate for the intended use. For an AI-powered legal assistant, this might include directives like “Provide information based on current laws and regulations,“ or “Avoid giving personal opinions or unverified information.“ Implementing guardrails is crucial in sensitive domains like legal services, where incorrect or harmful advice can have serious consequences. This technique helps ensure that the AI adheres to ethical standards and legal requirements, enhancing the reliability and trustworthiness of the system. By setting clear boundaries and expectations through your prompts, you reduce the risk of undesirable outputs and improve the overall quality of the AI‘s responses.

Incorrect

Response quality improvement

While improving response quality can enhance the model‘s outputs, it doesn‘t specifically address preventing harmful or misleading content. It focuses more on refining clarity, coherence, and relevance.

Chain-of-thought prompting

Chain-of-thought prompting encourages the model to explain its reasoning step-by-step. It aids in problem-solving but doesn‘t directly prevent undesirable or harmful outputs.

Experimenting with various prompt structures

Experimenting with different prompt structures may optimize responses but doesn‘t specifically implement measures to prevent the generation of harmful or misleading content.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/introducing-guardrails-in-knowledge-bases-for-amazon-bedrock

questions.text: A retail company is using a foundation model for personalized recommendations and is trying to minimize ongoing costs. They are choosing between fine-tuning the model or using Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG). What cost advantage does RAG provide over fine-tuning?

options.text: RAG requires less frequent re-training, leading to lower operational costs over time.
Fine-tuning is more cost-effective for short-term projects, while RAG reduces long-term operational costs.
Fine-tuning allows for better model accuracy, but RAG offers more cost-effective scalability.
RAG incurs higher storage costs but lower processing costs.

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

RAG requires less frequent re-training, leading to lower operational costs over time.

Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) combines pre-trained models with external knowledge retrieval systems. It eliminates the need for constant re-training because the system retrieves the latest information from external sources dynamically, rather than relying on model updates. This leads to lower ongoing operational costs, as RAG minimizes the need for expensive re-training sessions, which are typical in fine-tuning. Over time, RAG offers a more cost-effective solution by allowing the model to access up-to-date information without altering its underlying structure.

Incorrect

RAG incurs higher storage costs but lower processing costs.

RAG does not typically incur higher storage costs. It dynamically retrieves information, which may reduce storage requirements, but processing costs may vary depending on retrieval complexity.

Fine-tuning is more cost-effective for short-term projects, while RAG reduces long-term operational costs.

This statement is somewhat misleading. Fine-tuning is resource-intensive even for short-term projects, while RAG is designed to lower costs by reducing the need for frequent model updates over time.

Fine-tuning allows for better model accuracy, but RAG offers more cost-effective scalability.

Fine-tuning can improve model accuracy for specific tasks, but RAG doesn't directly focus on scalability as a cost-saving measure. Its key advantage is reducing the need for re-training, not necessarily offering cost-effective scalability.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/retrieval-augmented-generation

questions.text: Your team is training an AI model to predict healthcare outcomes for a diverse patient population. What practice should be implemented to ensure that the dataset leads to fair and equitable predictions for all demographic groups?

options.text: Focus on high-quality data from a specific geographic region
Use as much uncurated data as possible to capture all variations
Ensure the dataset is inclusive of a wide range of patient backgrounds
Ensure the dataset is curated from a single trusted hospital

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Ensure the dataset is inclusive of a wide range of patient backgrounds

To ensure fair and equitable predictions in healthcare outcomes, it‘s important to have an inclusive dataset that represents a diverse range of patient backgrounds, such as different ages, genders, ethnicities, socioeconomic statuses, and geographic locations. By including a variety of patients, the AI model will be able to generalize better and avoid bias toward any particular group. This helps ensure that the predictions made by the model are fair and applicable across all demographic groups, leading to better healthcare outcomes for everyone.

Incorrect

Ensure the dataset is curated from a single trusted hospital

Depending on data from just one hospital, even if it is trusted, limits the diversity of the dataset and could result in biased predictions that don't generalize well to other populations.

Focus on high-quality data from a specific geographic region

High-quality data is essential, but focusing on a single geographic region can lead to a dataset that doesn‘t reflect the diversity of patients from other regions, resulting in biased outcomes.

Use as much uncurated data as possible to capture all variations

While uncurated data can help capture variations, it may also introduce noise, errors, or biases that could affect the model's fairness. A curated and diverse dataset is preferable to ensure equitable predictions.
